chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khashshab from Ghiyath ibn Kalub from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon them both) that 'Ali (peace be upon him) used to say:

"It is more beloved to me that birds snatch me [away] than that I should speak upon the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) what he did not say. I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) say on the Day of the Trench: 'War is deception.' He said: 'Speak whatever you wish.'

key_terms.يَوْمِ الْخَنْدَقِ: The Day of the Trench (Battle of Khandaq)

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about war being deception during the Battle of the Trench?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights Imam Ali’s rigorous standards for narrating the Prophet’s words, using hyperbole to emphasize the sanctity of prophetic speech. It establishes 'War is deception' (*al-harb khud'ah*) as a foundational principle in Shia jurisprudence, where the Prophet’s command 'Speak whatever you wish' grants strategic flexibility in military contexts, allowing for tactical ambiguity or truthfulness as needed for victory.
